items.q: Frequencies are 3, 5, 7, 4. Find the cumulative frequencies.
items.imageAlt: A cumulative frequency ogive plotted from cumulative frequencies 3, 8, 15, 19 at upper class boundaries 10, 20, 30, 40, with a construction line showing how to read the median.
items.imageCaption: Half of 19 is 9.5 — read across, then down.
hints: Add each frequency to the running total of all frequencies before it.

items.q: What is plotted on the horizontal axis of a cumulative frequency graph?
hints: Recall which value from each class is used as the x-coordinate.
Each point is plotted at the top edge of its class interval.
Upper class boundaries

items.q: What is plotted on the vertical axis of a cumulative frequency graph?
hints: Recall what the running total represents.
The y-axis shows the running total of frequencies up to each class.
Cumulative frequency

items.q: Frequencies are 6, 4, 3. Find the cumulative frequencies.
hints: Add each frequency to the running total of all frequencies before it.

items.q: What does the final point on a cumulative frequency graph show?
hints: Think about what the running total has reached by the last class.
By the last class, every data value has been counted.
The total frequency

items.q: Should the cumulative frequency graph join the points smoothly?
hints: Think about how the running total changes gradually across the range of the data.
A smooth curve (or ruled line segments) is used to model the trend between plotted points.
Yes

items.q: Frequencies are 3, 5, 7, 4 across four classes. Which class number has the highest frequency?
hints: Compare the four frequencies directly — no cumulative total needed.
3, 5, 7, 4 — the largest is 7, in the 3rd class.
3rd

items.q: If the cumulative frequencies are 3, 8, 15, 19, find the class frequencies.
hints: Subtract each cumulative frequency from the one after it to get the class frequency.

items.q: If the final cumulative frequency is 19, what is the total frequency?
hints: The final cumulative frequency already counts every data value.
The last cumulative total IS the overall total.

items.q: If cumulative frequencies are 4, 9, 14, find the class frequencies.
hints: Subtract each cumulative frequency from the one after it to get the class frequency.

items.q: If the cumulative frequencies are 2, 6, 11, 18, find the class frequencies.
hints: Subtract each cumulative frequency from the one after it to get the class frequency.

items.q: If the graph reads 12 at an upper boundary, what does this mean?
items.a: 12 data values are at or below that boundary
hints: Recall what a cumulative frequency value counts.
It's a running total of every data value up to and including that boundary.
12 data values are at or below that boundary

items.q: If the total cumulative frequency is 40, what is the total number of data values?
hints: The final cumulative frequency already counts every data value.
The last cumulative total IS the overall total.

items.q: If the cumulative frequencies are 5, 12, 22, 30, 35, find the class frequencies.
hints: Subtract each cumulative frequency from the one after it to get each class frequency.

items.q: A data set has size 80. Which cumulative frequency gives the median?
hints: The median is at the halfway point of the data — divide n by 2.

items.q: A data set has size 80. Which cumulative frequency gives Q1?
hints: The lower quartile is a quarter of the way through the data — divide n by 4.

items.q: A data set has size 80. Which cumulative frequency gives Q3?
hints: The upper quartile is three-quarters of the way through the data — use 3n/4.

items.q: A data set has size 120. Which cumulative frequency gives the median?
hints: The median is at the halfway point of the data — divide n by 2.

items.q: A data set has size 120. Which cumulative frequency gives Q1?
hints: The lower quartile is a quarter of the way through the data — divide n by 4.

items.q: A data set has size 120. Which cumulative frequency gives Q3?
hints: The upper quartile is three-quarters of the way through the data — use 3n/4.

items.q: A data set has size 200. Which cumulative frequency gives the 90th percentile?
hints: A percentile position is found the same way as a quartile — multiply the total by the percentile as a decimal.
